title: Fix connections that stall under edge-triggered epoll
summary: A Linux echo server freezes after switching to EPOLLET. Make the sockets non-blocking and read until EAGAIN.

turns.user: switched epoll to EPOLLET and now bigger payloads just stop halfway. level triggered was fine. this is linux btw

assistant.body: Great observation! Edge triggering reports readiness once, at the moment new data arrives. Read 4096 bytes and return, and the rest stays in the kernel buffer, but no new notification comes until more data does. That is the stall. With edge triggering, the socket has to be non-blocking and read until read returns EAGAIN. accept works the same way: take every pending connection in one go.
Since listen_fd is non-blocking, the sockets accept returns inherit that flag, so the client side is fully covered. Handling a full send buffer with EPOLLOUT is a separate topic and is left out here.

turns.user: first connection works but from the second one everything freezes. strace shows it stuck in read

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Inheriting O_NONBLOCK through accept is BSD behaviour. On Linux, accept does not carry it over. The client stays blocking, so the read after the buffer is drained waits instead of returning EAGAIN, and the whole loop stops with it. The Linux-only accept4 takes SOCK_NONBLOCK and makes the socket non-blocking as it is accepted. _GNU_SOURCE is already defined at the top of the file.
sed -i '' 's/accept(listen_fd, NULL, NULL)/accept4(listen_fd, NULL, NULL, SOCK_NONBLOCK)/' src/net/echo.c
